title: Regenerate architecture.md's Feature Dependency Graph — 5 fabricated/renamed nodes, 3 missing features, 2 reversed edges

why: The mermaid graph (L237-285) uses 17 node identifiers; 5 don't exist under lib/features/ today. `auth` (L241, L263) was renamed to `account` — confirmed by account/domain/services/upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart:41's `UpgradeToCloudService`, which implements exactly the 'hard-tier upgrade flow' the doc still attributes to 'auth'. `stages` (L243, L251, L274), `parent_mode` (L255, L272), `track_setup` (L278), and `learning_order` (L249, L277) were folded into subdirectories of the unified `tracks/` feature (tracks/setup/, tracks/stages/, tracks/whole_curriculum_order/) — confirmed by tracks/setup/.../track_management_hub_screen.dart:31's `TrackManagementHubScreen`, which verbatim matches the doc's own 'track_setup | Track management hub' description. Three real, substantial features never appear as nodes at all: `sacred_time` (20 files), `tutoring` (34 files, e.g. tutor_audit_log_screen.dart:23 — a feature with its own cross-user tutor-access model, architecturally significant enough to warrant SR-5/FB-8 rules elsewhere in this audit's standard), and `tracks` (67 files) is only representable through its stale fragment names. Even two edges between correctly-named nodes run backwards: doc says `learning --> progress` (L247) but the only real import between these features is progress/journey_providers.dart:8 importing learning/, i.e. progress --> learning; doc says `scheduler --> dashboard` (L252) but the only real import is dashboard/dashboard_screen.dart:14 importing scheduler/, i.e. dashboard --> scheduler. A developer or AI coding agent using this graph to judge 'is it safe to change X without breaking Y' will reason from a diagram that inverts its own edges and omits a fifth of the real feature set.
recommendation: Regenerate the graph from real data: derive nodes from `ls lib/features/` and edges from grepping every `import 'package:learning_tracker/features/...'` in lib/features/ (excluding same-feature imports), pick a legible abstraction (e.g. treat tracks/* subdirectories as one node, or show only Rule-2-relevant edges), and add a make target that fails CI if the committed mermaid diagram's node set drifts from `ls lib/features/`.
acceptance_criteria: The mermaid graph's node identifiers exactly match `ls learning_tracker/lib/features/` (or a documented curated subset), with `auth` replaced by `account` and stages/parent_mode/track_setup/track_learning_order/learning_order removed or folded into a `tracks` node.
sacred_time, tutoring, and tracks appear as graph nodes with edges backed by an actual grep of cross-feature imports.
The learning<->progress and scheduler<->dashboard edges are corrected to their real direction or removed if no longer accurate.
A make/CI check derives the node set from `ls lib/features/` and fails with the diverging names if the committed graph's nodes don't match.

corrections: Two issues found, neither fatal to the core claim. (1) parent_mode's real successor is profiles/ (13 files: PIN screens, parent_dashboard_providers.dart) plus dashboard/domain/services/parent_dashboard_aggregator.dart — NOT tracks/ as the finding states; parent_mode is still correctly identified as a stale node, just mis-attributed as to where it went. (2) The '2 reversed edges' claim assumes strict import-direction semantics for the graph, but the doc's own Dependency Notes describe these exact edges with data-flow language ('learning...producing completion data that...progress...consume', 'scheduler...feeds dashboard') — under that stated semantics the arrows are consistent with the real import direction (consumer imports producer), so 'reversed' is a contestable interpretation, not a clean-cut error. Core fabricated/missing-node claims stand regardless.
